documents.name: Louvre Museum
documents.summary: The Louvre’s unmatched breadth lets one visit move from ancient civilizations to Renaissance masterworks inside a palace-scale museum.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The depth, range and concentration of globally important works make the Louvre an itinerary-changing museum even after aggressively discounting fame.

documents.name: Puy du Fou
documents.summary: Puy du Fou is a historical spectacle destination in Les Epesses, retained for distinctive visitor-experience quality.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Europe’s benchmark destination-scale historical spectacle park, built around technically ambitious live shows rather than rides.

audience.notes: Editorial destination-fit profile derived from the researched positive age span. Bands without positive evidence remain unknown rather than being treated as a positive match or a hard prohibition. Individual rides and activities may have stricter operator rules.

documents.name: Sentier Blanc-Martel
documents.summary: A full-day traverse inside the Grand Canyon du Verdon, alternating cliffside trail, river-level passages, giant staircases and long tunnels.
documents.whyWorthwhile: France’s most complete canyon hiking experience: the route spends hours inside the limestone gorge and remains distinctive well beyond any single viewpoint.

customFacets.hiking.crowding: Very popular in summer; the official tourism office reports that traffic disperses after hikers enter the gorge, but shuttle capacity and narrow passages still reward advance planning.

legacy-best-season.label: Best season
legacy-best-season.note: Spring or autumn in dry stable weather; avoid July and August heat and winter rockfall conditions.

legacy-access-point.label: Access point
legacy-access-point.note: The route begins at Chalet de la Maline and ends at Point Sublime / the Visitor Center; the point-to-point day normally requires the reserved seasonal shuttle or a prearranged taxi.

variants.name: Chalet de la Maline to Point Sublime — current detour

importantCondition.description: A municipal rockfall closure blocks the direct section from the Couloir Samson turnaround to Point Sublime. Follow RD23A for about 1 km and then GR49 to Point Sublime / the Visitor Center. The mapped detour shares about 0.84 km of live RD23A with vehicle traffic and briefly uses D952, including a segment tagged sidewalk=no, so use care on the road sections.

documents.name: Aiguille du Midi
documents.summary: A cable-car-accessed 3,842 m high-Alpine visitor complex above Chamonix with close Mont Blanc views.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of the strongest lift-accessed high-Alpine viewpoints in the Alps, tempered by serious queue, weather and altitude failure modes.

documents.name: Arc de Triomphe
documents.summary: The monument’s rooftop terrace turns the Champs-Élysées axis and Paris’s radiating avenues into a legible urban panorama.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The rooftop panorama and monumental architecture combine into a major Paris detour with a different city-reading payoff from the Eiffel Tower.

documents.name: Basilica of Notre-Dame de Fourvière
documents.summary: Lyon’s ornate hilltop basilica pairs a richly decorated interior with one of the city’s defining panoramas.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The combination of a genuinely striking interior and hilltop city context makes it a major Lyon detour rather than just a famous church.

documents.name: Chartres en Lumières
documents.summary: A free, long-season night route transforming Chartres’ cathedral, churches, bridges and civic buildings with light and sound.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of Europe’s strongest city-scale night environments: the architecture and public realm become a coherent visitor experience across an entire evening.

coreExperience.note: The illuminated route is predominantly visual.

weather.label: Dress for a long outdoor evening
weather.note: Cold or rain can materially shrink the route.

2026-season.note: The announced 2026 programme runs nightly in this window.

documents.name: Cité de l’espace
documents.summary: Cité de l’espace is a space discovery destination in Toulouse, retained for distinctive visitor-experience quality.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A destination-scale space visitor complex with full-size hardware, planetarium experiences and interactive interpretation.

documents.name: Dune du Pilat
documents.summary: Europe’s vast coastal dune rises between Atlantic water and pine forest, creating an unusually elemental walk and panorama.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The sheer moving-landscape scale is unusual enough to justify a dedicated detour rather than a generic beach stop.

documents.name: Eiffel Tower
documents.summary: Paris’s iron landmark is most rewarding as a structural ascent and open-air city panorama, not merely a photograph from below.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The combination of globally singular structure, scale and elevated Paris context repeatedly delivers a major-trip highlight.

documents.name: Futuroscope
documents.summary: Futuroscope is a immersive technology destination in Chasseneuil-du-Poitou, retained for distinctive visitor-experience quality.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A distinctive media, motion-simulator and spectacle park that remains unlike conventional coaster-led theme parks.

audience.notes: Editorial destination-fit profile derived from the researched positive age span. Bands without positive evidence remain unknown rather than being treated as a positive match or a hard prohibition. Individual rides and activities may have stricter operator rules.

documents.name: Gouffre de Padirac
documents.summary: A dramatic chasm leads to a guided underground-river journey with a boat section and immense decorated chambers.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The underground-river boat sequence and scale make Padirac one of France’s most distinctive cave visits.

documents.name: Hôtel des Invalides
documents.summary: The Invalides complex combines one of Europe’s major military-history collections with the Dome and Napoleon’s monumental tomb.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Collection depth plus the architectural and tomb component makes the complex a major history detour, not merely a famous burial site.

documents.name: Nausicaá Centre National de la Mer
documents.summary: Nausicaá Centre National de la Mer is a aquarium destination in Boulogne-sur-Mer, retained for distinctive visitor-experience quality.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A very large marine centre whose scale and immersive tank design materially exceed an ordinary city aquarium.

documents.name: Notre-Dame de Paris
documents.summary: The reopened Notre-Dame pairs its restored Gothic volume with unusually bright stonework, chapels and the accumulated history of Paris’s cathedral.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Current independent visitors consistently find the restored interior powerful enough to justify a major detour beyond the cathedral’s fame.

documents.name: Palace of Versailles
documents.summary: Versailles pairs the Hall of Mirrors and royal apartments with immense formal gardens and a full estate that rewards a deliberately planned day trip.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The combination of monumental interiors, garden scale and concentrated French royal history consistently justifies a major detour from Paris despite substantial crowd and stamina costs.

visualSignals.label: Style
visualSignals.value: French Baroque · classical French palace architecture

documents.name: Palais Garnier
documents.summary: A lavish 19th-century opera house whose staircase, foyers and decorative program make the daytime architectural visit worthwhile even without a performance.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The interior is one of Paris’s strongest historic architectural experiences and repeatedly earns a major detour on its own.

documents.name: Parc Astérix
documents.summary: Parc Astérix is a theme park destination in Plailly, retained for distinctive visitor-experience quality.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A high-quality theme park with strong coasters, family rides and enough themed character to justify travel beyond Paris.

audience.notes: Editorial destination-fit profile derived from the researched positive age span. Bands without positive evidence remain unknown rather than being treated as a positive match or a hard prohibition. Individual rides and activities may have stricter operator rules.

documents.name: Sainte-Chapelle
documents.summary: The upper chapel surrounds visitors with an extraordinary near-continuous wall of medieval stained glass.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The stained-glass room is singular enough to justify a major Paris detour despite the compact visit and security friction.

documents.name: Basilica of Sacré-Cœur de Montmartre
documents.summary: Montmartre’s white basilica combines a monumental interior with one of Paris’s classic hilltop settings.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its architecture and hilltop context are clearly worthwhile, but the crowd/tourist environment makes the experience less reliable than Paris’s A-tier interiors.

documents.name: Millau Viaduct
documents.summary: A vast cable-stayed bridge whose scale is best appreciated from the dedicated visitor viewpoints above the Tarn valley.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its exceptional scale and elegant landscape fit make it a clearly worthwhile corridor stop, especially for engineering and architecture interests.

documents.name: Moulin Rouge
documents.summary: Paris’s historic cabaret still delivers a high-production revue of dance, costumes, stage effects and classic cancan.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Current independent evidence supports the show itself as a genuinely memorable Paris nightlife experience, while value and comfort keep it below major-detour A.

legacy-booking-advice.label: Booking advice
legacy-booking-advice.note: Advance booking is strongly advisable because performances are fixed-capacity.

documents.name: Musée de l'Air et de l'Espace
documents.localName: Musée de l'Air et de l'Espace
documents.summary: Le Bourget's aviation museum combines a broad historic aircraft collection with Concordes, a 747, space exhibits and optional cockpit/aircraft access.
documents.whyWorthwhile: For aviation and space interests, the collection depth and access to iconic aircraft make this a clearly worthwhile dedicated trip outside central Paris.

legacy-accessibility-notes.label: Accessibility
legacy-accessibility-notes.note: The collection spans a very large site; some aircraft boarding and optional activities have separate access constraints.

documents.name: Panthéon
documents.summary: A monumental neoclassical interior and crypt turn France’s secular mausoleum into a focused architecture-and-history visit.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The combination of monumental space and nationally important burials makes it clearly worthwhile, though less singular than Paris’s A-tier icons.

documents.name: Curie Museum
documents.summary: A small free museum in the Curie laboratory complex preserves an unusually authentic setting for the history of radioactivity research.
documents.whyWorthwhile: For science-history travelers, the original institutional setting adds enough authenticity to clear the nearby publication floor.

documents.name: Palais-Royal Garden
documents.summary: A formal garden framed by arcades that provides an unusually calm, elegant pause beside the Louvre district.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It consistently clears the nearby-value floor as a beautiful, low-friction central-Paris pause without pretending to merit a dedicated cross-city trip.

documents.name: Tuileries Garden
documents.summary: A formal garden corridor between the Louvre and Concorde that works best as a high-quality walk, pause and city-space experience.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its landscape quality and route usefulness consistently make it worth using when nearby, but it is not a destination-scale detour by itself.
